newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Saudis, others see 97 call on OPEC 26.3 mln bpd.
newsitem.headline: Saudis, others see 97 call on OPEC 26.3 mln bpd.

text.p: Saudi Arabia and its Gulf allies see a call on oil from OPEC in 1997 at 26.3 million barrels per day (bpd), Gulf sources said on Thursday.
The Gulf sources said there was a general expectation of an increase next year in total world oil demand of 1.8 million bpd. One source called this "healthy demand".
This source said he saw 1.4 million bpd of new demand coming from emerging economies and 400,000 from the industrial nations of the Organization for Economic Cooperation ond Developmnent (OECD).
He said supply would rise 1.2 million bpd next year with 1.0 million of this from non-OPEC -including 400,000 to 500,000 from the North Sea- and 200,000 of OPEC condensates.
The sources said the Saudis and others expect prices to continue in a range of $20-25 for Brent next year.
This was a "new band" for the oil price which, apart from a spike during the Gulf War, had been in a range of $15-20 for Brent for the last 10 years.
The market could easily absorb revived Iraqi oil sales, the sources said.
"The oil market can absorb it without any problem", said one Gulf source. But "it is still uncertain when it will return"

"Another reason for optimisim is that we will finish this winter with very low stocks. This experience will lead oil companies to fill stocks whenever they can. There is no possibility at all, even with Iraq, of an overhang".
The sources were asked if a new price band of $20-25 was worrying for the Saudis and allies from the point of view of any impact on the global economy.
"The market can tolerate this new band", a source said, predicting minimum impact on inflation.
